# testenv

```go
import "github.com/colonel-byte/ansible-collection-zarf/internal/testenv"
```

Package testenv holds the scaffolding the end\-to\-end suites share: finding the repository root, and waiting on a cluster.

It is a trimmed copy of the \`test\` package this proof grew up in, in colonel\-byte/cargoship. What was dropped is everything that drove the cargoship CLI \-\- the binary lookup under build/, the command helpers and the staging\-directory handling \-\- because this repository builds no such binary. What is left is the two things the zarf suites actually call.

<a name="Bootstrap"></a>
### func [Bootstrap](<https://github.com/colonel-byte/ansible-collection-zarf/blob/main/internal/testenv/testenv.go#L52>)

```go
func Bootstrap() (Env, string, error)
```

Bootstrap chdirs into the repository root and reports the architecture, along with the root it moved into. The suites call this from TestMain: they spell every path \-\- testdata, playbooks, the collection \-\- relative to the repository root.

Arch is runtime.GOARCH. Zarf's own config.GetArch\(\) returns exactly that when no architecture has been forced on the command line, which is the only way these suites ever call it, so the zarf library is not worth a dependency here.
